entries.source: Arçelik MLCD_BLDC-BL Fault Diagrams (Rev 01, 08.10.2009, prepared by Engin BAYATLI, Recep SERÇE); Arçelik BX B7S BXBLED BL Washing Machine Service Manual No:1 (WTK92151W)

entries.meaning: F3 means a temperature sensor has a short or open circuit — but which sensor depends on the family: the environment/ambient sensor (RT SNR) on HB21F models, or the refrigerator sensor 1 (R1 SNR) on HRF-628 models. Both H
entries.source: Haier HB21FWRSS Refrigerator Service Manual (EDITION 2008-03-24); Haier HB21FNN Service Manual; Haier HRF-628AF6/IF6 Service Manual (Issue 2013-04-07, Ref1304S001V0); Haier HRF-663ISB2 Service Manual (Issue 20090416, Ref0904S016V0); Haier HRF-6631RG user manual

entries.meaning: F4 means the freezer sensor (F SNR) has a short or open circuit, per the Haier HRF-628AF6/IF6 service manual. It is an HRF-628-family-only code: the HB21F manuals have no F4, and the HRF-663 user manual's code list stops
entries.source: Haier HRF-628AF6/IF6 Service Manual (Issue 2013-04-07, Ref1304S001V0); Haier HRF-370F user manual; Haier HB21FWRSS Service Manual (EDITION 2008-03-24); Haier HRF-6631RG user manual

entries.meaning: F6 means a sensor has a short or open circuit — the icemaker sensor (ICE SNR) on HB21F models, or the defrost sensor (D SNR) on HRF-628 models. The two Haier service manuals define it differently per family, so the famil
entries.source: Haier HB21FWRSS Refrigerator Service Manual (EDITION 2008-03-24); Haier HRF-628AF6/IF6 Service Manual (Issue 2013-04-07, Ref1304S001V0); Haier HRF-663ISB2 Service Manual (Issue 20090416, Ref0904S016V0); Haier HRF-6631RG user manual

entries.meaning: F8 means the R2 sensor — the second refrigerator-compartment sensor, on the side wall of the refrigerator — has a short or open circuit, per the Haier HRF-628AF6/IF6 service manual. It is an HRF-628-family-only code.
entries.source: Haier HRF-628AF6/IF6 Service Manual (Issue 2013-04-07, Ref1304S001V0); Haier HRF-663ISB2 Service Manual (Issue 20090416, Ref0904S016V0); Haier HB21FWRSS Service Manual (EDITION 2008-03-24); Haier HRF-6631RG user manual

entries.meaning: E7 = Direction error: the Hall signal IC differs from the predicted signal for the direction of rotation. The motor stops and E7 is displayed; the alarm sounds for 10 seconds every 10 minutes and the display clears when the power is turned off and on.
entries.source: Daewoo Washing Machine Error Codes PDF, DD front-loader platform (E7 Direction); Daewoo DWC-ED1213 Service Manual (E7 Direction Error); Daewoo DWD-E1211R / DWD-E1211W Drum Washing Machine Service Manual (E7 Direction Error)

entries.meaning: H1 = Thermistor Dry OPEN/SHORT: the drying temperature sensor has failed. DWC-ED1213 causes: sensor temp. broken (change the sensor temp.) or connector problem (check the contact of the connector). Washer-dryer combos only.
entries.source: Daewoo DWC-ED1213 Service Manual (H1 sensor temp. dry disorder; ERROR MODE: Thermistor Dry OPEN/SHORT); Daewoo DWD-E1211R / DWD-E1211W Drum Washing Machine Service Manual (ERROR MODE: Thermistor Dry OPEN/SHORT)

entries.meaning: H4 = Wash Overheating: the wash temperature sensor reading is over 95 °C. DWC-ED1213 causes: wash heater working with no water supply (check water level) or wash sensor temp. broken (change the sensor temp.). Alarm 10 seconds every 10 minutes; display clears on power off/on.
entries.source: Daewoo Washing Machine Error Codes PDF, DD front-loader platform (H4 Overheating, 95 °C); Daewoo DWC-ED1213 Service Manual (ERROR MODE: Wash Overheating over 95 °C; H4 troubleshooting); Daewoo DWD-E1211R / DWD-E1211W Service Manual (H4 Wash Overheating over 95 °C); Daewoo DWD Service Manual (H4 Thermistor Wash Overheating)

entries.meaning: E2 = zero-crossing signal detection error: the system cannot detect the correct zero-crossing signal time interval (bad power-cable connection, faulty power supply, or faulty indoor PCB).
entries.source: Midea High Wall System Error Codes and Fault Diagnosis Guide (E2 section); Midea MSMBB-12CRDN1-MPOW Air Conditioner error table (E2, timer OFF, operation flash 3); Midea/Pridiom multi-zone inverter service document PWM093HX/PWM123HX/PWM183HX (E2 flowchart)

entries.meaning: E3 = indoor fan speed out of control: fan speed keeps too low (300 RPM) for a set time, then the unit stops and displays E3 (wiring, fan wheel/bearing, fan motor, PCB, or surge).
entries.source: Midea High Wall System Error Codes and Fault Diagnosis Guide (E3/F5 section); Midea MSMBB-12CRDN1-MPOW Air Conditioner error table (E3, timer OFF, operation flash 4); Midea/Pridiom multi-zone inverter service document PWM093HX/PWM123HX/PWM183HX (E3 flowchart)

entries.meaning: P0 = IPM malfunction / IGBT over-strong current protection: the voltage signal the IPM sends to the compressor drive chip is abnormal, so the display shows P0 and the AC turns off (wiring, IPM, outdoor fan motor, compressor, outdoor PCB, or surge).
entries.source: Midea High Wall System Error Codes and Fault Diagnosis Guide (P0 IPM Protection section); Midea MSMBB-12CRDN1-MPOW Air Conditioner error table (P0, timer flash, operation flash 1); Midea/Pridiom multi-zone inverter service document PWM093HX/PWM123HX/PWM183HX (P0 flowchart)

entries.meaning: P2 = high temperature protection of compressor top: protection trips at ≥120°C (248°F) and resumes at 105°C (221°F) (outdoor airflow, refrigerant system, blockage, protector, or outdoor PCB).
entries.source: Midea MSMBB-12CRDN1-MPOW Air Conditioner error table (P2, timer flash, operation flash 3); Midea/Pridiom multi-zone inverter service document PWM093HX/PWM123HX/PWM183HX (P2 120/105°C thresholds + diagnostic flowchart)

entries.meaning: E2 = indoor anti-freeze protection: the indoor coil dropped too cold in cooling or dry mode and the unit paused the compressor to stop it freezing. Restore return airflow and clean the coil; persistent E2 needs a technician.
entries.source: Gree Vireo owner's/troubleshooting manual; Gree R32 Slim Duct Mini Split System Owner's Manual; Gree U-Match Series DC Inverter Service Manual; Gree Soyal Service Manual

entries.meaning: E4 = compressor high discharge temperature protection: discharge temperature exceeded the safe limit (over 118°C) and the unit stopped to protect the compressor. Check airflow, then call a technician if it returns.
entries.source: Gree Vireo owner's/troubleshooting manual; Gree R32 Slim Duct Mini Split System Owner's Manual; Gree U-Match DC Inverter Series Owner's Manual; Gree Duct Type Split Air Conditioner Inverter Series Service Manual

entries.meaning: E5 = AC over-current protection: current exceeded the safe limit and the unit stopped. Causes are unstable supply voltage, low supply voltage under high load, or a blocked/dirty indoor coil. Restart once; persistent E5 is electrician/technician work.
entries.source: Gree Vireo owner's/troubleshooting manual; Gree R32 Slim Duct Mini Split System Owner's Manual; Gree Soyal Service Manual; Gree Vireo GEN3 Mini-Split Heat Pump Owner's Manual

entries.meaning: H1 = defrosting status: in heating mode the unit detected frost on the outdoor coil and paused heating to clear it. Fans stop during defrost, then the display returns to the setpoint and heating resumes. No action needed.
entries.source: Gree neo High-Wall Ductless Air Conditioning & Heating System Owner's Manual; Gree U-Match DC Inverter Unit manual; Gree 36000 BTU Triple-Zone Mini Split System Service Manual

entries.meaning: H6 = no feedback of the indoor fan motor: the control board is not receiving the fan's feedback signal, so the unit stops. Check for a blocked fan and restart once; persistent H6 needs a technician for the motor, connector, or board.
entries.source: Gree R32 Slim Duct Mini Split System Owner's Manual; Gree Split Air Conditioner User Manual; Gree GWH18TC-S3DBA1E Service Manual; Gree U-Match DC Inverter Series Owner's Manual

entries.meaning: F5 = defrost sensor malfunction: D SNR short circuit or open circuit. HB21F family only (HB21FWRSS, HB21FNN); HRF-628 defrost = F6, HRF-663 has no F5.
entries.source: Haier HB21FWRSS Refrigerator Service Manual (EDITION 2008-03-24); Haier HB21FNN Service Manual (breakdown table)

entries.meaning: E5 = water level sensor fault (HLT364XXQ, GWT900AW/GWT700AW/GWT800AW — call service) OR water temperature too high, over 60°C (HWM70-A — cool, then Start/Pause) OR Refresh drainage error, water not fully drained within 1 minute (HW70-B12929-S / HWD80/100/120-B14979 — clean pump filter, check drain hose; HW150-BP14986E variant: 3-minute window, spin to drain).
entries.source: Haier HLT364XXQ User Manual; Haier GWT900AW/GWT700AW/GWT800AW User Manual; Haier HWM70-A Washer User Manual; Haier HWD80/100/120-B14979 washer-dryer user manual (§9.2); Haier HW70-B12929-S user manual (§9.2); Haier official support article 'Haier Washer/Dryer Combo Fault Codes'; Haier HW150-BP14986E user manual (§9.2)

entries.meaning: E6 = the water level sensor is bad. Template top-load families only (7 manuals, identical wording). Same fault = E5 on HLT/GWT, FA on B14979.
entries.source: Haier HWM70-0588H user manual; Haier HWM65-0528 user manual; Haier HWM85-728 user manual; Haier HWM100-828A user manual; Haier HWM65-0566 user manual; Haier HWM80-0566 user manual; Haier HWM80-928NZP user manual

entries.meaning: E7 = communication fault: 'The communication is bad.' Four Haier washer manuals agree; remedy is after-sales service. Not Err7 (motor).
entries.source: Haier HWM70-0588H user manual; Haier HLT364XXQ User Manual; Haier GWT900AW/GWT700AW/GWT800AW User Manual; Haier HWM90DD User Manual

entries.meaning: E06 = temperature sensor in the dishwasher is faulty (P2 + P6 flashes on LED models). If the error is continuous and washing performance has reduced, close the dishwasher and get in touch with the authorized service.
entries.source: Beko BDIS16030 user manual (§9.1); Beko BDIN16550 user manual (§9.1); Beko BDIN38450C user manual (§9.1); Beko BDIN38550PF user manual (§9.1); Beko BDFN15330/B6B user manual (§9.1); Argos-support 3032 user manual (§9.1); Beko BDFS16030 user manual (§9.1); Beko BDFN26451 user manual (§9.1)

entries.meaning: E07 = flowmeter faulty (P2 + F1/F2 flashes on LED models). The error algorithm activates and the cycle ends; if continuous, cut off the electricity, close the valve, and get in touch with the authorized service.
entries.source: Beko BDIS16030 user manual (§9.1); Beko BDIN16550 user manual (§9.1); Beko BDIN38450C user manual (§9.1); Beko BDIN38550PF user manual (§9.1); Beko BDFN15330/B6B user manual (§9.1); Argos-support 3032 user manual (§9.1); Beko BDFS16030 user manual (§9.1); Beko BDFN26451 user manual (§9.1)

entries.meaning: E04 = continuous-fill fault: the machine keeps taking in water (inlet valve stuck open, valve triac short circuit, or control board fault). Turn the taps off first; if water still enters with the machine unplugged, the valve is mechanically faulty; if it stops, the triac/board is at fault.
entries.source: Arçelik B7S ARCD service document (Rev.00 10.04.2020, WTK platform) E4 flowchart; ukwhitegoods Beko WMA fault-code table (from information given to us from Beko) E4 row

entries.meaning: E07 = water level sensor (pressure sensor) error: the machine discharges every time it is turned on, or the programme does not start. Service checks: level-sensor socket and control-card KN2 socket fitted and secure, else repair sockets/cables, else replace the level sensor.
entries.source: Arçelik B7S ARCD service document (Rev.00 10.04.2020, WTK platform) E7 flowchart; ukwhitegoods Beko WMA fault-code table (from information given to us from Beko) E7 row

entries.meaning: E4 = indoor room temperature sensor (T1) open circuit or short circuit: sampling voltage below 0.06V or above 4.94V (wiring mistake, faulty sensor, or faulty indoor PCB).
entries.source: Midea High Wall System Error Codes and Fault Diagnosis Guide (E4/E5/F1/F2/F3 section); Midea MSMBB-12CRDN1-MPOW Air Conditioner error table (E4, timer OFF, operation flash 5); Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual 16122500000082 (E4, timer OFF, running lamp 5 flashes)

entries.meaning: F1 = outdoor room (ambient) temperature sensor T4 open circuit or short circuit: sampling voltage below 0.06V or above 4.94V (wiring mistake, faulty sensor, or faulty outdoor PCB).
entries.source: Midea High Wall System Error Codes and Fault Diagnosis Guide (E4/E5/F1/F2/F3 section); Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual 16122500000082 (F1, timer ON, running lamp 2 flashes); Midea Neola Midwall Inverters table (F1, T4, 2 flashes)

entries.meaning: F2 = outdoor condenser pipe (coil) temperature sensor T3 open circuit or short circuit: sampling voltage below 0.06V or above 4.94V (wiring mistake, faulty sensor, or faulty outdoor PCB).
entries.source: Midea High Wall System Error Codes and Fault Diagnosis Guide (E4/E5/F1/F2/F3 section); Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual 16122500000082 (F2, timer ON, running lamp 3 flashes); Midea Neola Midwall Inverters table (F2, T3, 3 flashes)

entries.meaning: F3 = discharging air / compressor discharge temperature sensor T5 open circuit or short circuit: sampling voltage below 0.06V or above 4.94V (wiring mistake, faulty sensor, or faulty outdoor PCB).
entries.source: Midea High Wall System Error Codes and Fault Diagnosis Guide (E4/E5/F1/F2/F3 section); Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual 16122500000082 (F3, timer ON, running lamp 4 flashes); Midea Neola Midwall Inverters table (F3, T5, 4 flashes)

entries.meaning: F1 (Gree wall-split) = indoor ambient (room) temperature sensor open circuit or short circuit (bad connection, faulty sensor, short from tripped parts, or faulty mainboard).
entries.source: Gree Split Air Conditioner User Manual (F1, cool indicator once/3s); Gree ETAC3-07HC230VA Terminal Air Conditioner User Manual (F1, indoor ambient open/short, STATUS flash once/3s); Gree NEO09AC115V1A Neo Ductless Instruction Manual (F1, indoor air thermistor); Gree Inverter AC Service Manual section 9.2 (F1/F2 tree)

entries.meaning: E1 = temperature sensor failure of the refrigerating (fresh-food) chamber (loose/contaminated connection, faulty sensor, or faulty main PCB).
entries.source: Midea Refrigerator User Manual: MERB345MG, MDRB470MG, MDRB521MGA; Midea MDRB521MIE02 User Manual; Midea MDRS619FIE / MDRS791MIE Side-by-Side User Manuals; Midea MRF23I5AST Built-In Manual; Midea MRQ23BCAST French Door Manual; Midea Service Manual REF MDRE411FGE01 (E1 tree)

entries.meaning: E4 = drain hose crimped or bent, or drain hose positioned too high (installation range 40–100 cm for the free end).
entries.source: Haier DW9-UFE3 User's Manual; Haier DW12-TFE1/DW12-TFE2 User Manual; Haier HDW12-SFE3 User Manual; Haier HDW12-TFE3SS User Manual; Haier DW12-EBE4TIS User Manual (40–100 cm installation range); Haier XF 4A4M4BX Manual (E4 leak contrast)

entries.meaning: E5 (Hisense portable) = unit full of water: the internal water container/tank has reached its limit and must be drained before the unit will run again.
entries.source: Hisense AP-12CR1SEPS User Manual; Hisense AP-10CR1SEPS User Manual; Hisense APC09 User Manual; Hisense Portable Air Conditioner Use and Installation Instructions (manuals.plus, multiple portable models); Hisense Portable Air Conditioner User Manual model B08LP358RZ

entries.meaning: E1 = the door is not closed properly (DW9/DW12/HDW12 families; buzzer: 10 short signals every 30 seconds). Series split: the newer XS family has no E1 (its fill fault is E2), and the US HDBL655AFS family's E1 is a longer-inlet-time fill code, not a door code.
entries.source: Haier DW9-UFE3 User's Manual (manualzilla); Haier DW12-TFE3-F User Manual (manualmachine); Haier DW12-TFE5 User Manual (manualmachine); Haier DW12-TFE 3-E User Manual FAQ (manua.ls); Haier DW12-TFE1/DW12-TFE2 User Manual (manualsdump); Haier HDW12-TFE3WH/SS User Manual (manualmachine)

entries.meaning: E3 = the drain hose is too low (DW9/DW12/HDW12 families; buzzer: 10 short signals every 30 seconds; installation range 40-100 cm for the hose free end) / the dishwasher does not drain water (XS family: drain pipe bent, trapped or blocked, filter clogged, siphon clogged). E3 is E4's mirror: too low is E3, too high/crimped is E4.
entries.source: Haier DW9-UFE3 User's Manual (manualzilla); Haier DW12-TFE3-F User Manual (manualmachine); Haier DW12-TFE5 User Manual (manualmachine); Haier HDW12-TFE3WH/SS User Manual (manualmachine); Haier XS 6B0M3PDB User Manual §19 (manua.ls); Haier XS 6B0S3FSB User Manual §19 (manua.ls); Haier DW12-EBE4TIS/DW12-EBM User Manual (40-100 cm drain-hose range)

entries.meaning: E5 = water-supply fault (DW9/DW12/HDW12 families; buzzer: 10 short signals every 30 seconds): check the water is turned on and the hose connected properly, the house supply is on with sufficient pressure, the supply hose is not crimped or bent, and the supply-hose filter is not clogged. Series split: the XS family has no E5 (its fill fault is E2).
entries.source: Haier DW9-UFE3 User's Manual (manualzilla); Haier DW12-TFE1/DW12-TFE2 User Manual (manualsdump, p.23); Haier DW12-TFE3-F User Manual (manualmachine); Haier DW12-TFE5 User Manual (manualmachine); Haier HDW12-TFE3WH/SS User Manual (manualmachine)

entries.meaning: E3 = heating exceed pre-set time: the heating element has worked for 60 minutes but the water temperature detected by the NTC has not reached the desired value, after which the drain pump runs until the flowmeter is motionless for 2 minutes, all other components stop, and the buzzer alarms for 30 seconds.
entries.source: Midea Technical Service Manual MDWEB1403MB-WA (midea.com, official); Midea Dishwasher Technical Service Manual, 7601S platform (E3 definition, machine reaction, inspection tree and troubleshooting table); Midea standard-version display-code dishwasher user manuals (E3: not reaching required temperature)

entries.meaning: E2 = temperature sensor failure of the freezing (freezer) chamber; wording varies by family (freezer drawer, freezing chamber, freezer room) but the sensor zone is identical, and it is not the fresh-food sensor (E1) or the ambient sensor (E7).
entries.source: Midea Refrigerator User Manual: MERB345MG, MDRB470MG, MDRB521MGA; Midea MDRB521MIE02 User Manual; Midea MDRB593FGE/MDRB593FGE46 Combined Refrigerator User Manual; Midea MDRF648FG Series Four Door User Manual; Midea MRF29D3AST/MRF29D3AWW/MRF29D3ABB French Door User Manual (midea.com); Midea MRF29D9BST French Door Series User Manual

entries.meaning: E5 = failure of the defrost sensor (defrost sensor detection circuit) of the freezing (freezer) chamber; it is a defrost fault, not the freezer temperature sensor (E2), and on four-door models it pairs with E4 (fresh-food defrost sensor) while on combi models it is the only defrost code.
entries.source: Midea Refrigerator User Manual: MERB345MG, MDRB470MG, MDRB521MGA; Midea MDRB521MIE02 User Manual; Midea MDRB593FGE/MDRB593FGE46 Combined Refrigerator User Manual; Midea MDRF648FG Series Four Door User Manual; Midea MRF29D3AST/MRF29D3AWW/MRF29D3ABB French Door User Manual (midea.com); Midea MRF29D9BST/MRF29D6AST French Door User Manuals

entries.meaning: E6 = communication error between the main control board and the display board; it is universal across checked refrigerator families with no scope split, and it is not CA (main board to ice-making board communication, French-door ice-maker models only).
entries.source: Midea Refrigerator User Manual: MERB345MG, MDRB470MG, MDRB521MGA; Midea MDRB521MIE02 User Manual; Midea MDRB593FGE/MDRB593FGE46 Combined Refrigerator User Manual; Midea MDRF648FG Series Four Door User Manual; Midea MRF29D3AST/MRF29D3AWW/MRF29D3ABB French Door User Manual (midea.com); Midea MRF29D9BST French Door Series User Manual; Midea Service Manual REF MDRE411FGE01 (midea.com, E6 section 11.3)

entries.meaning: E3 = compressor low-pressure protection, including refrigerant-lacking protection and refrigerant-collecting (recovery) mode; the system stops when suction pressure falls below the protection value (floor-standing service manual: below -41C equivalent), and E3 during refrigerant recovery is a normal mode, not a fault.
entries.source: Gree One-Way Cassette Air Conditioner Owner's Manual section 7 (E3: compressor low pressure protection, refrigerant lack protection and refrigerant collecting mode); Gree Floor Standing Type Split Air Conditioner Units Service Manual section 28 (E3 system low pressure protection, all models, suction below -41C, seven-cause tree); Gree UMA30HP230V1ACS U-Match Installation Manual Table 6.1 (E3: same wording); Gree Zone Controller Owner's Manual (E3: compressor low pressure protection, low refrigerant)

entries.meaning: F3 = outdoor ambient temperature sensor open circuit or short circuit; unusually, wall-split and U-Match numbering agree on F3, so there is no platform split for this code.
entries.source: Gree NEO09AC115V1A Neo Ductless Instruction Manual (F3: Outdoor Air Temp. Thermistor, Bad Connection or Outdoor Ambient Sensor Failure); Gree One-Way Cassette Owner's Manual section 7 (F3: outdoor ambient temperature sensor open/short circuited); Gree UMA30HP230V1ACS U-Match Installation Manual Table 6.1 (F3: outdoor ambient temperature sensor error); Gree ME33-42/G Owner's Manual p.30 (F3: outdoor ambient temperature sensor error)

entries.meaning: F1 = freezer (F) sensor disconnection or short circuit, shown as Lo for disconnection and Hi for short circuit; while faulty, the compressor and freezer fan cycle 25 minutes ON / 25 minutes OFF, and the code clears automatically once the sensor reads normal.
entries.source: Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual section 6 (F1: F-sensor disconnection/short, 25 min ON/OFF control); Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual section 5 (F1 check point: resistance across terminals after separating CN15, replace freezer-compartment F-sensor); Daewoo FRS20 User Manual section 5 (same F1 definition, CN8/CN15); Daewoo IWD/KAN58 repair manual section 7.1 (F1: freezer compartment sensor)

entries.meaning: r1 = refrigerator-compartment (R) sensor disconnection or short circuit, shown as Lo for disconnection and Hi for short circuit; while faulty, control falls back to the ambient-temperature work-rate table, and the code clears automatically once the sensor reads normal.
entries.source: Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual section 6 (r1: R-sensor disconnection/short, ambient work-rate fallback, auto-clear); Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual section 5 (r1 check point: resistance after separating CN14, replace refrigerator-compartment sensor); Daewoo FRS20 User Manual section 5 (r1: Lo/Hi, CN7/CN14); Daewoo IWD/KAN58 repair manual section 7.1 (r1: refrigerator compartment sensor)

entries.meaning: E2 = the dishwasher does not fill with water (XS family only; short audio signal, or 2 LED flashes with a 5-second pause on display-less models). Series split: on DW9/DW12/HDW12 families E2 is paired with E6 as 'contact the nearest authorized service center' with no fault meaning, so DW/HDW owners must not follow the XS fill diagnosis as their E2 meaning.
entries.source: Haier XS 6B0M3PDB User Manual §19 (manua.ls, p.45); Haier XS 6B0S3FSB User Manual §19 (manua.ls); Haier DW9-UFE3 User's Manual (manualzilla, E2/E6 service line); Haier DW12-TFE1/DW12-TFE2 User Manual (manualsdump, E2/E6 service line)

entries.meaning: E3 = temperature sensor failure of the meat & fish zone (variable-temperature drawer). SCOPED: E3 exists only on models with a meat & fish zone or variable-temperature drawer; French-door MRF29D3 and four-door MDRF648FG manuals list no E3, so owners of those models must not use this page.
entries.source: Midea Refrigerator User Manual: MERB345MG, MDRB470MG, MDRB521MGA; Midea MDRB521MIE02 User Manual; Midea MDRB593FGE/MDRB593FGE46 Combined Refrigerator User Manual; Midea variable-temperature-chamber refrigerator user manual (German edition)

entries.meaning: E4 = failure of the defrosting sensor in the refrigerating (fresh-food) chamber. SCOPED: E4 exists only on four-door / variable-temperature-chamber families, paired with E5 (freezing defrost sensor); the common combi families (MERB345MG, MDRB470MG, MDRB521MGA, MDRB521MIE02, MDRB593FGE) have no E4 at all.
entries.source: Midea MDRF648FG Series Four Door Refrigerator User Manual; Midea variable-temperature-chamber refrigerator user manual (German edition); Midea variable-temperature-chamber refrigerator user manual (manuals.plus); Midea Service Manual REF MDRE411FGE01 (midea.com, E4 in troubleshooting group 11.2)

entries.meaning: F4 = the sensor at the bottom of the refrigerating (fresh-food) ice maker fails. SCOPED: F4 exists only on French-door models with a refrigerating-chamber ice maker; it is a sensor fault, distinct from F5 (ice maker fails to turn over ice), F6 (initialization failure), and EE (freezer ice-maker bottom sensor).
entries.source: Midea MRF29D3AST/MRF29D3AWW/MRF29D3ABB French Door User Manual (midea.com); Midea MRF29D9BST French Door Series User Manual; Midea MRF29D6AST French Door Refrigerator Freezer User Manual; Midea Service Manual REF MDRE411FGE01 (midea.com, F4 in troubleshooting group 11.2)

entries.meaning: F5 = the refrigerating (fresh-food) ice maker fails to turn over (release) ice. SCOPED: F5 exists only on French-door models with a refrigerating-chamber ice maker; it is a mechanical harvest failure, distinct from F4 (bottom sensor), F6 (initialization failure), and EP (freezer ice-maker turn-over failure).
entries.source: Midea MRF29D3AST/MRF29D3AWW/MRF29D3ABB French Door User Manual (midea.com); Midea MRF29D9BST French Door Series User Manual; Midea MRF29D6AST French Door Refrigerator Freezer User Manual

entries.meaning: E8 = diverter (distributary) valve fault: the machine does not detect the diverter valve signal for 15 seconds or accurate diverter positioning within 60 seconds. SCOPED: E8 is valid only for models equipped with a diverter valve (alternative washing function); during a washing program E8 is set off only after the program ends.
entries.source: Midea Technical Service Manual MDWEB1403MB-WA (midea.com, official, diverter-validity note); Midea Dishwasher Technical Service Manual, 7601S platform (E8 definition, 15s/60s thresholds, machine reaction, inspection tree); Midea standard-version display-code dishwasher user manuals (E8: open circuit or break of distributary valve)

entries.meaning: F3 = defrosting return happened by time limit instead of by the D (defrost) sensor, so the defrost cycle timed out and Pre-cool mode in defrosting mode is deleted. Series split: 80-minute limit on FRS-2011/2031, FRS20 and FR-530NT/590NT; 50-minute limit on FRSU21DFV.
entries.source: Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual section 6 (F3: defrosting-return by 80-min time limit, Pre-cool deleted); Daewoo FRS20 User Manual section 5 (F3: 80-min limit, defrost heater resistance check); Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual section 5 (F3: 50-min limit); Daewoo IWD/KAN58 repair manual section 7.1 (F3: last defrost reset over time, not via freezer sensor; check heater and thermal fuse)

entries.meaning: F2 (wall-split) = indoor evaporator (indoor coil/tube) temperature sensor open circuit or short circuit. Series split: on U-Match / fan-coil families F2 instead means the outdoor condenser temperature sensor.
entries.source: Gree NEO09AC115V1A Neo Ductless Instruction Manual (F2: Indoor Coil Temp. Thermistor, Bad Connection or Indoor Coil Sensor Failure); Gree One-Way Cassette Owner's Manual section 7 (F2: indoor evaporator temperature sensor open/short circuited); Gree GJC08BU-A6NRNJ2A Window Instruction Manual (F2: indoor evaporator temperature sensor malfunction); Gree ETAC3-07HC230VA Terminal Manual (F2: indoor tube sensor, STATUS flash twice every 3s); Gree UMA30HP230V1ACS U-Match Table 6.1 (split: F2 = condenser temperature sensor error)

entries.meaning: F4 (wall-split) = outdoor condenser (outdoor coil/tube) temperature sensor open circuit or short circuit. Series split: on U-Match families F4 instead means the compressor discharge temperature sensor.
entries.source: Gree NEO09AC115V1A Neo Ductless Instruction Manual (F4: Outdoor Coil Temp. Thermistor, Bad Connection or Outdoor Coil Sensor Failure); Gree One-Way Cassette Owner's Manual section 7 (F4: outdoor condenser temperature sensor open/short circuited); Gree GJC08BU-A6NRNJ2A Window Instruction Manual (F4: outdoor condenser temperature sensor malfunction); Gree UMA30HP230V1ACS U-Match Table 6.1 (split: F4 = discharge temperature sensor error)

entries.meaning: F5 (wall-split) = compressor discharge (exhaust) temperature sensor open circuit or short circuit, not to be confused with E4 (high discharge temperature protection trip). Series split: on U-Match families F5 instead means the wired-controller temperature sensor.
entries.source: Gree NEO09AC115V1A Neo Ductless Instruction Manual (F5: Compressor Discharge Temp. Thermistor, Bad Connection or Discharge Sensor Failure); Gree One-Way Cassette Owner's Manual section 7 (F5: outdoor discharge temperature sensor open/short circuited); Gree UMA30HP230V1ACS U-Match Table 6.1 (split: F5 = temperature sensor error of wired controller); Gree ME33-42/G Owner's Manual p.30 (split: F5 = wired controller temperature sensor error)

entries.meaning: rt = room/ambient-temperature (RT) sensor disconnection or short circuit, shown as Lo for disconnection and Hi for short; the sensor sits on the main PCB, checked by voltage at point 'A' (0.5V–4.5V normal, 0V short, 5V disconnected), and the code clears automatically once the sensor reads normal.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual §5; Daewoo FRS20 User Manual §5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual §6; Daewoo FR-530NT/590NT Manual §6; Daewoo IWD/KAN58 repair manual §7.1

entries.meaning: d1 = defrost (D) sensor — the evaporator sensor — disconnection or short circuit (Lo/Hi); while faulty, defrost return is governed by a time limit (30 min most families, 40 min FR-530NT/590NT) instead of the sensor, and the code clears automatically once the sensor reads normal.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual §5; Daewoo FRS20 User Manual §5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual §6; Daewoo FR-530NT/590NT Manual §6; Daewoo IWD/KAN58 repair manual §7.1

entries.meaning: C1 = abnormal refrigeration cycle: compressor works for over 3 hours while the D-sensor temperature stays above -5°C; the manuals' check point is refrigerant leakage, control is normal running, and the code terminates when the D-sensor falls below -5°C while the compressor is off.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual §5; Daewoo FRS20 User Manual §5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual §6; Daewoo FR-530NT/590NT Manual §6; Daewoo FR-3502 Service Manual §6; Daewoo FRS-T20DA manual §6

entries.meaning: dr = refrigerator (R) door sensed open for more than 1 hour; check first whether the door is actually open, ajar, or blocked, then whether the R-door switch is stuck reporting open; door-switch sensing is suspended while active and the code terminates automatically once an open-and-close is sensed.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual §5; Daewoo FRS20 User Manual §5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual §6; Daewoo FR-3502 Service Manual §6; Daewoo FRS-T20DA manual §6; Daewoo IWD/KAN58 repair manual §7.1

entries.meaning: dF = freezer (F) door sensed open for more than 1 hour; check first whether the door is actually open, ajar, or blocked by food or ice, then whether the F-door switch is stuck reporting open; door-switch sensing is suspended while active and the code terminates automatically once an open-and-close is sensed.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual §5; Daewoo FRS20 User Manual §5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual §6; Daewoo FR-3502 Service Manual §6; Daewoo FRS-T20DA manual §6; Daewoo IWD/KAN58 repair manual §7.1

entries.meaning: F6 (wall-split) = limit / decrease frequency due to overload (overload, high-temperature resistance): all loads keep operating normally while the compressor's operating frequency is decreased; not a sensor fault, not a stop fault; U-Match has no F6, GMV VRF F6 is a compressor-2 discharge-sensor fault.
entries.source: Gree GWH Series Service Manual, Display Method entry 17; Gree Soyal Service Manual, same display table entry 17; GREE Inverter AC Service Manual (Bora inverter), same display table entry 17; Gree Livo+ LIVS12HP115V1A Service Manual §9.1

entries.meaning: F8 (wall-split) = decrease frequency due to overcurrent: all loads keep operating normally while the compressor's operating frequency is decreased, because the input supply voltage is too low or the system pressure is too high and the system is overloaded; not a sensor fault, not a stop; U-Match has no F8, GMV VRF F8 is a discharge-sensor fault.
entries.source: Gree GWH Series Service Manual, Display Method entry 18; Gree Soyal Service Manual, same display table entry 18; GREE Inverter AC Service Manual (Bora inverter), same display table entry 18; Gree Livo+ LIVS12HP115V1A Service Manual §9.1

entries.meaning: F9 (wall-split) = decrease frequency due to high air discharge (high exhaust/discharge temperature limit): all loads keep operating normally while the compressor's operating frequency is decreased, because of overload or temperature too high, insufficient refrigerant, or a malfunctioning electric expansion valve (EKV); not F5 (sensor) and not E4 (protection trip); U-Match has no F9, GMV VRF F9 is a compressor-5 discharge-sensor fault.
entries.source: Gree GWH Series Service Manual, Display Method entry 19; Gree Soyal Service Manual, same display table entry 19; GREE Inverter AC Service Manual (Bora inverter), same display table entry 19; Gree Livo+ LIVS12HP115V1A Service Manual §9.1

entries.meaning: H4 = system overload protection (system abnormal, overload / high-temperature resistance): when the tube temperature gets too high — outdoor heat-exchanger temperature in cooling, indoor heat-exchanger temperature in heating — the protection activates; in cooling/drying the compressor stops while the indoor fan keeps running, and in heating the whole unit stops; manual causes: outdoor temperature too high when cooling, insufficient outdoor air circulation, refrigerant flow malfunction; GMV VRF H4 is fan drive PFC protection.
entries.source: Gree GWH Series Service Manual, Display Method entry 34; Gree Soyal Service Manual, same display table; Gree GWHD Linge Wind Series Service Manual (GWHD12A6ND31A), malfunction-analysis item 6; Gree UMA30HP230V1ACS U-Match Table 6.1; Gree ME33-42/G Owner's Manual p.30

entries.meaning: E9 = a button/touch key held down for more than 30 seconds — a stuck touch key on touch-key models only; manual's fix: check for foreign objects on the button, clean it, then power on again; NOT in the 7601S platform valid-code list.
entries.source: Midea Dishwasher Technical Service Manual (manuals.plus fa1e variant); Midea WQP8-W3908T-CN Dishwasher Quick Start Guide; Midea Dishwasher Technical Service Manual, 7601S platform

entries.meaning: E8 (XS/XF) = water heating element not working correctly or filter plate clogged; manual's fix: clean the filter plate. SPLIT: XPI8D9FFB E8 = leak (drain pump runs permanently, anti-overflow device on).
entries.source: Haier XS 6B0M3PDB User Manual §19; Haier XS 6B0S3FSB User Manual §19; Haier XF 4A4M4BX-80 User Manual §19; Haier XPI8D9FFB User Manual p.153 (split)

entries.meaning: E18 (XS) = water-level problems; check clogged filter plate, clean the filter plate; if it continues or recurs, contact the Technical Assistance Centre. Not Bosch E18 (drain fault). Display-less models: 18 flashes.
entries.source: Haier XS 6B0M3PDB User Manual §19; Haier XS 6B0S3FSB User Manual §19; Haier XF 4A4M4BX-80 User Manual §19

entries.meaning: F6 = the initialization of the refrigerating (fresh-food) ice maker fails — the maker never completes its start-up sequence. Not F5 (harvest/turn-over failure) and not E0 (freezer initialization failure).
entries.source: Midea MRF29D3AST/AWW/ABB User Manual fault table (midea.com); Midea MRF29D9BST French Door Series User Manual fault table (manuals.plus); Midea MRF29D6AST French Door Refrigerator Freezer User Manual fault table (manuals.plus)

entries.meaning: EP = the freezer ice maker fails to turn over (release) its ice — a mechanical harvest failure of the freezer maker. Freezer counterpart of F5. On single-ice-maker families the same code is worded generically as the (only) ice maker failing to drop/separate ice.
entries.source: Midea MRF29D9BST French Door Series User Manual fault table (manuals.plus); Midea MRF29D6AST French Door Refrigerator Freezer User Manual fault table (manuals.plus); Midea MDRS925CIE46M User Manual fault table (midea.com); Midea MRQ23B4AST Owner's Manual fault table (manuals.plus)

entries.meaning: EE = the sensor at the bottom of the freezer ice maker fails. Freezer counterpart of F4 (fresh-food bottom sensor). On single-ice-maker families the same code is worded generically as 'ice maker sensor fault'.
entries.source: Midea MRF29D9BST French Door Series User Manual fault table (manuals.plus); Midea MRF29D6AST French Door Refrigerator Freezer User Manual fault table (manuals.plus); Midea MDRS925CIE46M User Manual fault table (midea.com)

entries.meaning: CC = the defrosting sensor in the ice-making chamber fails. Not C9 (chamber temperature sensor) and not E5/E4 (freezer/fresh-food defrost sensors).
entries.source: Midea MRF29D3AST/AWW/ABB User Manual fault table (midea.com); Midea MRF29D9BST French Door Series User Manual fault table (manuals.plus); Midea MRF29D6AST French Door Refrigerator Freezer User Manual fault table (manuals.plus)

entries.meaning: C9 = the sensor in the ice-making chamber fails (MRF29D9BST English table: the temperature sensor in the ice-making chamber). Not CC (chamber defrost sensor). One French-language D9BST copy words C9 as a defrost sensor; the English tables distinguish CC from C9 and are followed here.
entries.source: Midea MRF29D3AST/AWW/ABB User Manual fault table (midea.com); Midea MRF29D9BST French Door Series User Manual fault table, English (manuals.plus); Midea MRF29D6AST French Door Refrigerator Freezer User Manual fault table (manuals.plus)

entries.meaning: CA = the communication between the main control board and the ice-making board fails. NOT E6: E6 is the display-board to main-control-board link — a different link, different boards, different repair.
entries.source: Midea MRF29D3AST/AWW/ABB User Manual fault table (midea.com); Midea MRF29D9BST French Door Series User Manual fault table (manuals.plus); Midea MRF29D6AST French Door Refrigerator Freezer User Manual fault table (manuals.plus); Midea MRQ22D7AST fault table (manualsfile)

entries.meaning: dH = the home-bar door switch is defective — the small home-bar door in the refrigerator door is sensed open for an hour or longer. Not dr (refrigerator door) or dF (freezer door). Only applies to dispenser models that have a home bar.
entries.source: Daewoo FRS-20 Fridge Freezer Operating Instructions / FRS-U20 Service Manual, section 4-10-2 Dispenser Model (CLED Display of Front PCB), Error Code table (manuals.plus / scribd copies)

entries.meaning: Et (Ft on FRS-2011/2031) = level switch error — no pulse sensed, supply mode skipped.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-20 User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual section 6

entries.meaning: Eu = full-ice switch error — drop motor rotates only 90 degrees.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-20 User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual section 6

entries.meaning: EI = ice-maker I-sensor disconnected (Lo) or shorted (Hi); CN11 check.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-20 User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual section 6

entries.meaning: Ea = ice-drop motor malfunction (test-switch check). EA also covered: level-sensor timing fault, ice maker paused.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-20 User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual section 6

entries.meaning: ES = dispenser micro-switch error — sensed continuously for 1 minute; dispenser stops.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-20 User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual section 6

entries.meaning: EF = flow-sensor error — no pulse while water should flow; timed supply fallback.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-20 User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual section 6

entries.meaning: Eg = I-sensor temperature does not rise 5 minutes after water supply.
entries.source: Daewoo FRSU21DFV User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-20 User Manual section 5; Daewoo FRS-2011/2031 Service Manual section 6

entries.meaning: EC = BLDC wash-pump fault — reveal subcode L0-L6 by 5-second button hold.
entries.source: Midea Dishwasher Service Manual MDWEF1433DW-SS-WA (midea.com); Midea Dishwasher Service Manual MDWEB1403MB-WA (midea.com); Midea Dishwasher Technical Service Manual (manuals.plus); De'Longhi DEDW650S User Guide (p.25); Midea standard-version manual 6710028212 (platform split)

entries.meaning: Ed = communication failure main board to display board, 20-second trigger.
entries.source: Midea Dishwasher Technical Service Manual (manuals.plus, 7601S family); Midea Smart Dishwasher with WiFi User Manual model 340607; Midea MDC22P2ASS Dishwasher User Manual

entries.meaning: Ed = communication failure main PCB to display PCB, open/broken wiring.
entries.source: Hisense HSCE14FS/HSCE14FB Instruction Manual (manualspro); Hisense HSCM15FS User's Operation Manual page 49 (manualslib)

entries.meaning: FH (wall-split) = limit/decrease frequency due to antifreezing; keeps running slower.
entries.source: Gree GWH Series Service Manual display table entry 20; Gree Soyal Service Manual same entry; GREE Inverter AC Service Manual (Bora) same entry

entries.meaning: P3 (indoor display) = outdoor temperature too low protection; thresholds split by family.
entries.source: Midea service manual section 9.1/9.3; Midea Luna Series DC Inverter manual section 9.1; Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual row 23; Midea R410A Duct Type Owner's Manual row 20

entries.meaning: E06 = the machine cannot start — the door is not closed or the lock hasn't engaged. Close firmly and retry.
entries.source: Arçelik Beko B13 Service Handbook; Beko user manuals (BM3WFSU48415WPBB2); ukwhitegoods WMA table

entries.meaning: E09 = water intake problem — fill time exceeded. Check the water tap is fully open, the inlet hose isn't kinked, and the inlet filter isn't blocked.
entries.source: Beko B13 Service Handbook; Beko user manuals; ukwhitegoods WMA table

entries.meaning: E10 = pressure switch (water level sensor) error. Call a service technician — no user repair step.
entries.source: Beko B13 Service Handbook; ukwhitegoods WMA table

entries.meaning: E11 = drain pump fault — water won't drain or drain time exceeded. Clean the drain pump filter, check the drain hose.
entries.source: Beko B13 Service Handbook; Beko user manuals; ukwhitegoods WMA table

entries.meaning: E12 = unbalanced load at spin — the machine reduces or skips spin. Redistribute the load evenly and retry.
entries.source: Beko B13 Service Handbook; ukwhitegoods WMA table

entries.meaning: E17 is a warning, not an error: excessive foam detected — programme may end without spinning. Reduce detergent, run rinse-only cycles.
entries.source: Arçelik Beko B13 Service Handbook (E17 marked 'warning, not error'); Beko user manuals

entries.meaning: E18 is a warning, not an error: unbalanced load — spin not initiated. Redistribute laundry evenly and retry.
entries.source: Arçelik Beko B13 Service Handbook (warning, not error); Beko BM3WFSU48415WPBB2 user manual

entries.meaning: E29 = the machine has too little water — intake fault. Check the water tap, inlet hose, and inlet filter.
entries.source: Beko user manuals; ukwhitegoods WMA table

entries.meaning: E8 = the water level is not reached within 8 minutes (top-loaders). Check the tap is fully open, hose isn't kinked, inlet valve filter isn't blocked.
entries.source: Haier top-loader user manuals (HWM series); Haier service documentation

entries.meaning: F3 = temperature sensor error. The manuals prescribe no user step — contact after-sales service.
entries.source: Haier HW80/HW100/HW120-B14979, HW70B1426S, HW70-B14929-S, HW7014829 user manuals

entries.meaning: F4 = heater error. The manuals prescribe no user step — contact after-sales service.
entries.source: Haier front-load user manuals (F-series tables)

entries.meaning: F7 = motor error. The manuals prescribe no user step — contact after-sales service.
entries.source: Haier front-load user manuals (F-series tables)

entries.meaning: FA = water level sensor error. The manuals prescribe no user step — contact after-sales service.
entries.source: Haier front-load user manuals (F-series tables)

entries.meaning: FC = communication error between boards (top-loaders). Power off/on once; if it returns, contact service.
entries.source: Haier top-loader user manuals

entries.meaning: Unb = unbalanced load — the machine tried to rebalance and the spin didn't reach full speed. Redistribute laundry and retry.
entries.source: Haier user manuals (unbalance handling)

entries.meaning: E5 = motor error (front-load E-series). Restart the programme; if it reoccurs, call a service technician.
entries.source: Hisense E-series troubleshooting table (manual 820685); Hisense HWGA9014 user manual

entries.meaning: E6 = heating error (front-load E-series). Restart the programme; if it reoccurs, call a service technician.
entries.source: Hisense E-series troubleshooting table (manual 820685); Hisense HWGA9014 user manual

entries.meaning: E7 = temperature sensor error (front-load E-series). Restart the programme; if it reoccurs, call a service technician.
entries.source: Hisense E-series troubleshooting table (manual 820685); Hisense HWGA9014 user manual

entries.meaning: E8 = 3D sensor error (front-load E-series). Restart the programme; if it reoccurs, call a service technician.
entries.source: Hisense E-series troubleshooting table (manual 820685); Hisense HWGA9014 user manual

entries.meaning: E9 = water at the bottom of the machine (Total Aqua Stop). Switch off and on; if it reoccurs, call a service technician.
entries.source: Hisense E-series troubleshooting table (manual 820685); Hisense HWGA9014 user manual

entries.meaning: E10 = water level sensor error (front-load E-series). Restart the programme; if it reoccurs, call a service technician.
entries.source: Hisense E-series troubleshooting table (manual 820685); Hisense HWGA9014 user manual

entries.meaning: E11 = water overflow: programme interrupted, water pumped out. Restart — but if it keeps filling, close the tap and call a technician.
entries.source: Hisense E-series troubleshooting table (manual 820685); Hisense HWGA9014 user manual; ASKO W4086C; Gorenje partners manuals

entries.meaning: E12 = motor control error (front-load E-series) — the motor's control, not the motor. Restart; if it reoccurs, call a technician.
entries.source: Hisense E-series troubleshooting table (manual 820685); Hisense HWGA9014 user manual

entries.meaning: E22 = error while locking the door — closed but cannot lock. Off/on, restart programme; if it reoccurs, call a technician.
entries.source: Hisense E-series troubleshooting table (manual 820685); Hisense HWGA9014 user manual

entries.meaning: E23 = error while unlocking the door — closed but cannot unlock. Turn off/on; if it reoccurs, call a technician.
entries.source: Hisense E-series troubleshooting table (manual 820685); Hisense HWGA9014 user manual

entries.meaning: H5 = water temperature error in wool/delicate course — 45 °C or higher. Alarm 10 s per 10 min; clears on power off/on. Thermistor wash: technician.
entries.source: Daewoo DWC-1011W service manual p.33; Daewoo front-loader troubleshooting guide pp.33-34

entries.meaning: H6 = heater wash error — temperature fails the 15-minute rise test (2 °C at ≤42 °C standard, 1 °C above). Alarm 10 s per 10 min; clears on power off/on.
entries.source: Daewoo DWC-1011W service manual p.33; Daewoo front-loader troubleshooting guide pp.33-34

entries.meaning: H8 = heater wash overheating — heater rises 5 °C+ in 30 s with no water in tank. Do not run heated washes; call a technician.
entries.source: Daewoo DWC-1011W service manual p.33; Daewoo front-loader troubleshooting guide pp.33-34

entries.meaning: PFE = pump filter error — clogged drain pump filter, pump fault, too much/unsuitable detergent, or hose above 1 m. Reset: Power → SPIN → Start/Pause.
entries.source: Daewoo front-loader troubleshooting guide p.34; DWC-ED1232 operation table; DWD-HC1011/HD9414 service manuals p.31

entries.meaning: E7 on a Gree air conditioner means MODE CONFLICT — two or more indoor units on the same outdoor unit are set to incompatible modes (one heating while another cools).
entries.source: GREE R32 Slim Duct Mini Split System Owner's Manual, error table row 7; Gree One-Way Cassette Owner's Manual, error table row 7; Gree R410A Service Manual, common-codes list; GREE Vireo GEN3 Mini-Split Owner's Manual, error table (multi-zone mode-conflict wording)

entries.meaning: E8 on a Gree air conditioner (duct / cassette / slim-duct families) means ANTI-HIGH TEMPERATURE PROTECTION — the system has tripped on high temperature, and the cassette diagnostic shows the outdoor yellow indicator flashing 6 times with a 1-second pause.
entries.source: GREE R32 Slim Duct Mini Split System Owner's Manual, error table row 8; Gree One-Way Cassette Owner's Manual, error table row 8; Gree Ceiling Cassette Owner's Manual, diagnostic codes (E8, High Temperature Resistant Protection, outdoor yellow 6 flashes + 1 sec off)

entries.meaning: E9 on a Gree air conditioner (duct / cassette families) means FULL WATER PROTECTION — the indoor unit's condensate level has reached the full-water state (drain tray / water-level device).
entries.source: GREE R32 Slim Duct Mini Split System Owner's Manual, error table row 9; Gree One-Way Cassette Owner's Manual, error table row 9; Gree R410A Service Manual, common-codes list; Gree Super Free Match Series manual, indoor-unit table

entries.meaning: EE on a Gree air conditioner means the main control board's memory chip has failed — loading EEPROM malfunction / outdoor main-control memory-chip malfunction.
entries.source: GREE R32 Slim Duct Mini Split System Owner's Manual, error table row 18; Gree One-Way Cassette Owner's Manual, error table row 16; Gree Vireo diagnostic list (EE, outdoor yellow 11 flashes + 1 sec off); Gree 1309378 Owner's Manual, error table (EE, main control; ee, drive)

entries.meaning: E0 on a Midea air conditioner (indoor display, timer OFF, running lamp 1 flash) means indoor unit EEPROM parameter error — the indoor PCB main chip does not receive feedback from the EEPROM chip.
entries.source: Midea High Wall System Error Codes and Fault Diagnosis Guide, E0/F4 section; Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual, error table row 1; Midea R410A Middle Static Pressure Duct Type Owner's Manual, Table 7-3 row 1; Midea service manual, section 9.1

entries.meaning: E5 on a Midea air conditioner (current-generation indoor display, timer OFF, running lamp 6 flashes) means the evaporator coil temperature sensor (T2) is open circuit or short circuit.
entries.source: Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual, error table row 5; Midea R410A Middle Static Pressure Duct Type Owner's Manual, Table 7-3 row 5; Midea High Wall System Error Codes and Fault Diagnosis Guide, E4/E5/F1/F2/F3 section; Midea service manual, section 9.1

entries.meaning: E8 on a Midea air conditioner (indoor display, timer OFF, running lamp 9 flashes) means communication malfunction between two indoor units — and it is TWINS-MODEL ONLY.
entries.source: Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual, error table row 8; Midea R410A Middle Static Pressure Duct Type Owner's Manual, Table 7-3 row 8; Midea Air Conditioner Error Codes page, cassette/ducted/underceiling current-generation indoor table

entries.meaning: E9 on a Midea air conditioner (indoor display, timer OFF, running lamp 10 flashes) means 'other malfunction of twins model' — and it is TWINS-MODEL ONLY, the residual twins code next to E8.
entries.source: Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual, error table row 9; Midea R410A Middle Static Pressure Duct Type Owner's Manual, Table 7-3 row 9; Midea Air Conditioner Error Codes page, cassette/ducted/underceiling current-generation indoor table

entries.meaning: EE on a Midea air conditioner (indoor display, timer OFF, running lamp 8 flashes) means water-level alarm malfunction — the indoor unit's water-level device has alarmed (drain tray / float / pump circuit on duct/cassette units fitted with one).
entries.source: Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual, error table row 7; Midea R410A Middle Static Pressure Duct Type Owner's Manual, Table 7-3 row 7; Midea Air Conditioner Error Codes page, cassette/ducted/underceiling current-generation indoor table

entries.meaning: F6 on a Midea air conditioner (indoor display, timer ON, running lamp 7 flashes) means T2b sensor error.
entries.source: Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual, error table row 16; Midea R410A Middle Static Pressure Duct Type Owner's Manual, Table 7-3 row 16; Midea Air Conditioner Error Codes page, cassette/ducted/underceiling current-generation indoor table

entries.meaning: F7 on a Midea cassette air conditioner means the indoor unit has lost communication with the auto-lifting panel — the motorized grille that lowers for filter cleaning.
entries.source: Midea Air Conditioner Error Codes and Troubleshooting Guide (Midea 24-page technical document; current-generation Cassette/Ducted/Underceiling indoor units) + Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual (Duct and Ceiling Type error table) + Midea Multi Outdoor Unit Service Manual, Revision C ODMI-E-1606 (MCH2U-18PHH2, MCH3U-27PHH2, MCH4U-36PHH2, MCH5U-48PHH2; cassette optional lift panel rows)

entries.meaning: F8 on a Midea cassette air conditioner means the auto-lifting panel itself is faulty — its motor or mechanism is not responding.
entries.source: Midea Air Conditioner Error Codes and Troubleshooting Guide (Midea 24-page technical document; current-generation Cassette/Ducted/Underceiling indoor units) + Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual (Duct and Ceiling Type error table) + Midea Multi Outdoor Unit Service Manual, Revision C ODMI-E-1606 (MCH2U-18PHH2, MCH3U-27PHH2, MCH4U-36PHH2, MCH5U-48PHH2; cassette optional lift panel rows)

entries.meaning: F9 on a Midea cassette air conditioner means the auto-lifting panel is not fully closed — usually after filter cleaning or if something blocks it.
entries.source: Midea Air Conditioner Error Codes and Troubleshooting Guide (Midea 24-page technical document; current-generation Cassette/Ducted/Underceiling indoor units) + Midea Air Conditioner Owner's Manual (Duct and Ceiling Type error table) + Midea Multi Outdoor Unit Service Manual, Revision C ODMI-E-1606 (MCH2U-18PHH2, MCH3U-27PHH2, MCH4U-36PHH2, MCH5U-48PHH2; cassette optional lift panel rows)

entries.meaning: E27 = check the water drain hose installation. It is not the pump filter (E05) and not a leak (E12).
entries.source: Beko user manuals BM3WFSU38213WPBB (doc 1911862482, EN, 20.03.24), BM3WFSU39413W, BM3WFSU48415WPBB2, BM1WFSU36233WPBB, BM3WFU410415WPBB, BM1WFSU37233WPBB (doc 1911863176_AA_UK_EN), BMW9149DB, BMGWU4941B, B3WFU4741WBG, WUE9726XBW, WUE7626XBWST, B5WF U78415 WB — failure-code table row 'E27: Check the water drain of the machine. See Connecting the drain hose to the drain section'

entries.meaning: E84 = the machine can't pair over Bluetooth (BLE) with the HomeWhiz app. Re-run the app pairing; it is not a Wi-Fi or main-board fault.
entries.source: Beko user manuals BM3WFSU38213WPBB (doc 1911862482, EN, 20.03.24), BM3WFSU39413W, BM3WFSU48415WPBB2, BM1WFSU36233WPBB, BM3WFU410415WPBB, BM1WFSU37233WPBB (doc 1911863176_AA_UK_EN), BMW9149DB, BMGWU4941B, B3WFU4741WBG, WUE9726XBW, WUE7626XBWST, B5WF U78415 WB — failure-code table row 'E84: BLE connection cannot be established. Check it, try connecting it. See HomeWhiz Feature and Remote Control Function section'

entries.meaning: E7 = ambient temperature sensor error on most Midea fridge families — but on two models it means a temperature detection circuit fault instead. Check your model.
entries.source: Midea MRQ23P4AST French-Door Bottom Mount User Manual (midea.com official PDF, v.A 07-2021); Midea MDRS791MIE/MDRS791MIC Side-by-Side User Manual (manuals.plus); Midea MERB345MG/MDRB470MG/MDRB521MGA User Manual (manuals.plus); Midea MDRB593FGE/MDRB593FGF Bottom Freezer Manual (manualspro.net); Midea MRQ23BCAST French Door Manual (manuals.plus); Midea MRF23I5AST Built-In Manual (manuals.plus); Midea MDRB521MIE02 Manual (manua.ls); Midea MDRS925CIE46M Manual (midea.com official UK PDF); series-split wording from Midea MDRS619FIE Side-by-Side Manual (manuals.plus) and Midea MDRF632FGF46APD Manual (manualslib.com)

entries.meaning: EH = the humidity (moisture) sensor has failed. Same fault, two wordings — 'humidity sensor' on some models, 'moisture sensor' on others.
entries.source: Midea MRQ23P4AST French-Door Bottom Mount User Manual (midea.com official PDF, v.A 07-2021); Midea MRQ23BCAST French Door Series User Manual (manuals.plus); Midea MRF29D3AST/MRF29D3AWW/MRF29D3ABB French Door User Manual (manualsdir.com); Midea MRF23I5AST Built-In Refrigerator User Manual (manuals.plus); moisture wording from Midea MDRF632FGF46APD User Manual (manualslib.com) and Midea MERF402FIE User Manual (manuals.plus)

entries.meaning: E0 = ice maker fault on ice-maker-equipped Midea fridges. Not the air-conditioner E0 (EEPROM) — same code, different appliance, different fault.
entries.source: Midea MDRS925CIE46M Side-by-Side User Manual fault table (midea.com official UK PDF); Midea MRS26D5AST Side-by-Side User Manual ERROR CODES table, version E 01-2024 (manuals.plus); Midea Service Manual REF MDRE411FGE01, BMF No Frost Series, E0 troubleshooting tree (midea.com official PDF)

entries.meaning: L3 = freezer fan fault — the freezer fan has stopped working. Check L4 too: that's the fan running at the wrong speed, a different code.
entries.source: Midea MDRS925CIE46M Side-by-Side User Manual fault table (midea.com official UK PDF); Midea MDRB600MIC46P User Manual fault table (midea.com official PDF); Midea MRS25I7BST Side-by-Side User Manual fault table (manuals.plus); fan steps from Midea Service Manual REF MDRE411FGE01, BMF No Frost Series (midea.com official PDF)

entries.meaning: L4 = freezer fan speed is abnormal — the freezer fan is turning, but at the wrong speed. Different from L3, which means the fan has stopped.
entries.source: Midea MDRS925CIE46M Side-by-Side User Manual fault table (midea.com official UK PDF); Midea MDRB600MIC46P User Manual fault table (midea.com official PDF); Midea MRS25I7BST Side-by-Side User Manual fault table (manuals.plus); fan steps from Midea Service Manual REF MDRE411FGE01, BMF No Frost Series (midea.com official PDF)

entries.meaning: L5 = condenser fan fault — the fan that cools the condenser near the compressor has failed. Not the freezer fan (that's L3/L4).
entries.source: Midea MDRS925CIE46M Side-by-Side User Manual fault table (midea.com official UK PDF); Midea MDRB600MIC46P User Manual fault table (midea.com official PDF); Midea MRS25I7BST Side-by-Side User Manual fault table (manuals.plus)

entries.meaning: L6 = condenser fan speed is abnormal — the condenser fan is turning, but at the wrong speed. Different from L5, which means the fan has stopped.
entries.source: Midea MDRS925CIE46M Side-by-Side User Manual fault table (midea.com official UK PDF); Midea MDRB600MIC46P User Manual fault table (midea.com official PDF); Midea MRS25I7BST Side-by-Side User Manual fault table (manuals.plus)

entries.meaning: Defrost-component fault on Daewoo's Spain-built no-frost combis (ERF-364/367 series) — defrost heater or temperature fuse open, or heavy evaporator frost; freezer red LED blinks twice.
entries.source: Service Manual "No-Frost Combi-Refrigerator ERF-364_367 ALL AR-EU MODELS" — Daewoo Electronics Manufacturing Espana S.A., 2003 (covers ERF-364A..EU / ERF-367A..EU, ERF-384A..EU / ERF-387A..EU, ERF-394A..EU / ERF-397A..EU, ERF-414A..EU / ERF-417A..EU, plus R-600a ..AR range); Service Manual "No-Frost Combi-Refrigerator", Model ERF-416A — Daewoo Electronics Manufacturing Espana, S.A. (same D1/D2/R1/RT LED-error table; table verified via document crawls after one failed direct PDF fetch)

entries.meaning: High temperature alarm in the freezing chamber on Midea freezer lines (bottom-freezer BMF No Frost, upright and chest freezers) — an alarm, not a sensor fault.
entries.source: Midea Service Manual REF MDRE411FGE01 (midea.com official PDF), Section 9.7 "Error code and solutions" — BMF No Frost Series; Market Model MDRE411FG, Product Model HD-390RWEN BI, Product Code CE-BCD300WX-JT 22031020011081 (direct PDF download from midea.com, 2026-10-31; §9.7 explicitly labelled "Note: Midea full common fault code"); Midea Upright Freezer Single Door Series User Manual (manuals.plus), model MDRU385MTE46; Midea MFR411W User Manual (manualsfile.com); Midea MF411W Upright Freezer User Manual (manuals.plus); Midea Chest Freezer Instruction Manual (worten.es, AF_Manual_Chest Freezer, 30/01/2018)

entries.meaning: Touch-button fault on Haier HDBL655/HDBL865 24-inch built-in dishwashers: a button registered as pressed for longer than 30 seconds; cause is water or substance on the button.
entries.source: Haier User Manual, Dishwasher HDBL655AFS (also covers HDBL655AFW, HDBL655AFB; 24-inch built-in, US, July 2015), section ERROR CODES, p.31; Haier User Manual, HDBL865ATS 24-inch Built-In Dishwasher (trilingual EN/FR/ES), section ERROR CODES, p.32. Support: Haier Consumer Help Line 1-877-377-3639

entries.meaning: Water tank installation failure on Midea BMF No Frost (MDRE411FG) and SBS No Frost (MDRS925CIE46M) refrigerators — reseat the tank, check seat terminals and seat switch.
entries.source: Midea Service Manual REF MDRE411FGE01 (midea.com official PDF), Section 9.7 Error code and solutions — BMF No Frost Series, Market Model MDRE411FG / HD-390RWEN BI / CE-BCD300WX-JT 22031020011081; Midea Service Manual — SBS No Frost Series, Section 8.6, Market Model MDRS925CIE46M / SA-BCD695WZ-JT / 92031050Z05922 (both midea.com official PDFs); corroborated by ZLINE RSM-W / RFM-W user manuals (rebadged Midea platform)

entries.meaning: Series-split code: digitron top-loads (XQS/WM/HWM) — power voltage too high, unplug and wait for normal voltage; HWM200 series — communication failure between show board and power board, contact Customer Care.
